title: The Judgment of Satan and Demons
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
searchTerms: The Judgment of Satan and Demons
definition: The judgment of Satan and demons is the certain final punishment of rebellious spiritual powers by God. Their rebellion will not continue forever; they will be cast into eternal judgment.
summary: The judgment of Satan and demons is the certain final punishment of rebellious spiritual powers by God. Their rebellion will not continue forever; they will be cast into eternal judgment.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the conquering King who will finally judge Satan and every demonic power. His victory guarantees that evil will not have the last word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture teaches that Satan and demons are headed for judgment. Hell was prepared for the devil and his angels, and Revelation shows the devil finally cast into the lake of fire.

The judgment of demons shows that spiritual rebellion has an appointed end. Evil may rage, deceive, and oppress for a time, but it cannot escape the justice of God.

Some fallen angels are described as kept for judgment, showing that God already holds rebellious powers under His sovereign authority. Their doom is certain even before the final day arrives.

Christ’s victory guarantees this judgment. The God of peace will crush Satan, and the risen King will bring every enemy under His feet.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Believers may become discouraged by the persistence of evil. This doctrine reminds them that darkness is temporary and judged. Satan’s future is not uncertain.

It also brings sobriety. Hell and final judgment are real. Spiritual rebellion does not end in freedom, but in eternal punishment under the righteous judgment of God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not envy rebellion or fear evil as though it will last forever. Stand firm in Christ, resist darkness, and trust God’s justice. Let the certainty of Satan’s judgment strengthen perseverance, worship, and hope in the final victory of Jesus.
